I was even to be the -- on duty on the night between the 10th and 11th of June but because it was Bajram and that is a major Bosniak holiday, that is a major Islamic holiday, I had asked Anto Pranjic, my colleague, to replace me, that is to be on duty that day, so I was working until the very last day, until the very last moment, that is I should have been but I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I want to ask you now about what happened on the day of the takeover so you can -- the usher can take the document back from you.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: That day, that is that morning, I was in front of the mosque in my neighbourhood, that is in my street, in Donji Varos. I didn't go for a prayer because I thought I'd visit all the mosques and I'd see some people and so on. However, sometime around half past 4.00 or rather sometime between half past 4.00 and five past 5.00, I heard a moving column of motor vehicles, a sizeable one, moving from the direction of Banja Luka. I assumed that it was a column bringing forces to take over the power, because -- I'd like to mention incidentally that people often talked how power would be taken over and then people would come up with the dates, but nothing ever happened on those dates, I don't know why. So that I -- that evening I had also heard that story that there would be the takeover but I paid no attention because I thought it would be just like all those dates that were mentioned earlier. But that morning, I realised it, and I hid behind a house near the mosque and they passed by and I realised that the day has come -- had come, and the column was -- so in front of the column was a police official vehicle, followed by an APC, or some army vehicle, and then two or three jeeps, and then followed by two or three buses -- I'm not quite sure about that -- with, I suppose, a special unit and then finally followed by an armour combat vehicle. They stopped for a while near the mosque and then they went on towards the centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you pause for a moment?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: There was attempt to --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you if you could have, please, the map with the photographs -- I'm not sure -- which has already been exhibited, P2123. Sir, just before we look at the actual map, I can assure you, Your Honours, that he doesn't speak English. He's got everything marked on it. Can you just tell us for the photographs, can you identify what photographs 2 and 3 are?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: This is the police station where I worked, number 3 is -- it's the factory, but I'm not sure about this. I think it's one of the halls in the sawmill in Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Don't worry about that, but number 2 is the police station in which you worked. And can you identify what number -- photograph number 6 --

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: And this below it is a factory hall after all.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. And number 6, can you identify? Don't worry if you can't. It's not important.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: I am not 100 per cent certain, so I would not like to be venturing a guess here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Can we go --

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Really not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we go back to the town plan? Can you indicate to us from which direction the convoy, as it were, came from?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: From the direction of Banja Luka and Celinac. This is Donji Varos and the mosque, I believe, is around here, yes, right here. They passed here, the convoy came from there and they passed through here down this street towards the centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. And you were, you say, standing in Donji Varos, near the mosque?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, near the mosque, at a bridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, you can put the map away now. All right, sir, you saw this convoy arrive. As it was the religious holiday of Bajram, were most of the Muslims at the mosque?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, most of the Muslims were at the mosque, but there were a number of different mosques in different locations too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So what did you do when you saw this convoy arrive?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, first, I kept one of the armed boys from doing anything [as interpreted], then I entered the mosque, and I addressed the people praying there, my neighbours, friends and the people there, I told them that there would be no prayer because a convoy had entered Kotor Varos, and the war had broken out. I said it was inevitable that there would be a takeover. I told them to disperse, and whoever felt unsafe staying in town should leave and get on their way, I said. And those who wanted to stay could stay. It was up to them, I said, to decide whether they felt safer inside or outside the town. I wished them all the best, obviously.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So what did you personally do?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: I left immediately. I went to my house. I spoke to my brother and told him to join me. I took some clothes, a backpack, which I filled with food, medicines and some ammunition. I took my rifle, the rifle that I'd signed for officially, and together with some neighbours, I set out for Ravne, an area between four and five kilometres away from Donji Varos, across the Vrbanja river.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Page 48, line 25, I think what he said was he kept one of the armed boys from firing a shot or shooting or something like that rather than doing anything. I believe that's what was said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What we'd like to know, witness, whether you said I kept one of the armed boys from doing anything or I kept one of the armed boys from firing a shot? The question of interpretation -- of translation that you need to clear up for us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I prevented that young man from using that weapon, from firing. I was trying to prevent an incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, you said that you set out for Ravne and can you just have for a moment again the map P2120? Can we see Ravne in -- yes, you're just pointing to it at the top left of the map.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: The River Vrbanja, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In a moment I'm going to ask you to look at a video of the area and we can see not Ravne itself but at least the landscape. All right. Now, you set off for Ravne, did you go anywhere before you got to Ravne?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, no. I didn't. I went straight to Ravne.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did Mr. Djikic, the President of the SDA, amongst others, go with you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He did. Haza Djikic [phoen] was also at the mosque. He was about to pray for the Bajram prayer. He had a flat in Carsija but his mother is a neighbour of mine, so every Bajram he'd visit his mother and pray near Donji Varos near where she lived. So that's why he was at the mosque that day. He was in two minds whether to join us or not, probably because his wife and two daughters had remained in the flat in Carsija, but his cousin, Senad Djikic told him you must come with us, there is nothing for you to ponder, you must not say. So he joined us eventually but he was very much in two minds and I think it was his cousin's influence that decided it for him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I think you set up, as it were, your headquarters or centre of operations in Ravne but did you visit other villages around this period of time on the 11th of June?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I didn't set up headquarters right away. That was several days later. I went to the neighbouring village, Vranica. I knew people there and I went to see them, to tell them about what had happened in Kotor Varos, in Carsija. I arrived in the village, some young men were there on the football pitch preparing for a traditional Bajram tournament, a traditional local tournament which was the usual thing to do around that time in the region and the teams were preparing for the tournament. Well you know the atmosphere, holiday atmosphere. I told the boys that the tournament would not take place. I told about what had happened and I asked them to please take it seriously. I told them what the situation was and to set up guards immediately around the village and to be on their guard. To take things seriously because hard times were coming, I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, once you were in Ravne, were you joined by other people?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When the forces entered Carsija, a number of people for their own reasons, for reasons of their own personal safety, came over, obviously some of them had family there, some may have been born there, but had a house in town. For example, Suljo, a neighbour of mine who was from Ravne, he had a house in Donji Varos but he left the house with his wife and daughter and came to his father's place in Ravne. There were many cases like his.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, did the Serbs themselves send any kind of troops or police to Ravne?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: No. No. They didn't send any kind of troops. I know this for a fact. People who had arrived from Donji Varos told me this. They told me that 15 or 20 minutes after I'd left the house, my house was surrounded by members of the special unit, but they didn't send any of the police or military troops. They did send over certain people to negotiate, messengers from the Crisis Staff, from Carsija, those people came to Ravne and I personally talked to one of them Karin Dizdar [phoen], who, at the beginning as a Muslim was a member of the Crisis Staff. That was at the beginning. I'm not sure if there were any other Muslims who were members of the Crisis Staff. This only lasted for a very brief while so they didn't send any units or troops, they sent civilians to negotiate.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, eventually, did -- was there a group with you as the head that formed the resistance in Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: This group was set up on that day. That's when we started setting it up but prior to that, there was nothing, no unit, no formation like that. It was from that day on, following the takeover, that's when certain people started organising themselves, people I knew, my friends, approached me, and we used this group to set up our headquarters, and people suggested that I should become the commander of that staff, and that was a Territorial Defence of Kotor Varos municipality. That's how we referred to it. It was made up of Muslims and Croats, according to the different localities that were represented in the body so that's how this body worked roughly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Before we go into the details of that, I'd like you, please, to have a look at a video of the area and just identify certain landmarks, if you can.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is part of Mr. Inayat's long video and we've split a segment and I think, I hope, the audiovisual unit have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think they have it because it was already on the monitor a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's very dark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I suggest you put it on video evidence. It's much better.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir I'm just going to ask you to stop if you recognise landmarks. Can you tell us what that is. Can you stop the video, please, what we're looking at?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would just like to ask a question. Am I speaking any slower now? Is this better? Is it slower than it used to be, before I start answering the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think you're doing fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Sadikovic, do you recognise that building? If you don't, say so straight away.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: I believe this is Donji Varos, Vrbanja to the left, and this to the right, this is the asphalt road. I think this is a place, one of the halls, factory halls in Donji Varos. Can we just zoom in a little? Just to make sure this is not the mosque? Because if there is a mosque there, then it's Vrbanjci. This white building here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I'm not sure, we'll have to see what the camera man, mainly Mr. Inayat, did. Continue, playing, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the answer is not really.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: I believe this is Vrbanjci, the school building and the surrounding buildings, and the River Vrbanja over there. I think this is the Vrbanjci local commune.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know what --

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: This is Vecici. This was after the aggression against Kotor Varos, that's when the footage was taken, also part of Vrbanjci, of the local commune of Vrbanjci. This is Vecici, the mosque in Vecici, the minaret had been torn down and across the way from there, Grabovci and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we stop and just go back a little bit because I think we've missed the mosque. Mr. Sadikovic, if you can say stop when we can see the mosque in the picture?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Stop. This is the mosque without the minaret, understandably, because it had been torn down.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you -- I know it's difficult, but we can't see your finger pointing, regrettably, sir, can you just tell us roughly if we look at it, whereabouts in the picture? Is it in the foreground?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: This -- you can see the dome here, the copper dome.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if I may just be permitted to go and see what he's pointing at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps if we rewind a little bit more, I think it's more visible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a bit unclear but yes, you can see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. Now let's go forward.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You've moved it. Here, this, stop. We can just try to zoom in a little bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, can the camera or one of the cameras focus on the witness and his monitor and then I ask him to point on the monitor where he is seeing the mosque, please? I don't know if that is possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Unless -- is it that building at the back, we can see a flat-roofed building, or what looks like a flat-roofed building, carrying down the road that we can see in the foreground and just by the trees? Is that what you're indicating? I wonder if the usher -- it's probably easier if the usher goes and has a look and sees what he's indicating at.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, there is no minaret so this may be a bit confusing but I know the place really well. Although you can't see it clearly, here, this is the mosque, except without the tower, the minaret which had been pulled down. There is only the dome left and parts of the original mosque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm seeing it and I have no doubt what he is referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good, that's all right. In that case, if Your Honours are all seeing it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman isn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm not sure I am either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps you can leave your place, go next to the witness and he will show you what he is pointing at.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I thought it was that building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, all right. If we can continue playing the video, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ackerman, thank you, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If you can indicate, I know we don't see Ravne itself but roughly where it was when you see the nearest place?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you, this footage here shows Vrbanjci local commune. This is at least ten kilometres away from Ravne. Therefore, I can orientate myself on the road leading to Banja Luka. I could point it out roughly but it's not in this footage because you can't see it here. There is a great distance between the two places. The place we are showing here, and Ravne. Ravne lies in the direction of Banja Luka heading out towards Vrbanjci towards Casa [phoen] and the town to the left of the Vrbanja river and above Gornji Varos between three and four kilometres further on down the road from Donji Varos.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Is it on -- is it in the hills itself?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I don't think so. I think we are still far off the mark. This footage is showing the Vrbanjci local commune and then further down towards Donji Varos, but in order for me to point out Ravne, you would need to have some footage of the town itself. And then I could point it out to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mind, never mind?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Or I could tell you how far it was from Donji Varos if at least we had that, if we had the factory.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Don't worry, just tell us what we are looking at, when you recognise a landmark.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: This is panoramic view of a section of the local commune of Vrbanci. I think that's what most of your footage is showing. Well, this is -- we are getting closer to the town itself. This is the urban area of Kotor Varos. This is Carsija. This is a neighbourhood we refer to as blocks. Here is the saw mill and there is Ravne over there. If we just rewind the tape a little and then move it a little to the left, a bit more to the left, please, stop here. Roughly speaking, Ravne, this hill side over there, this is the River Vrbanja, this is Donji Varos, this is where the river runs, to the left is the Kotor neighbourhood, Kukavica, Duratovci, and then above that, that's where Ravne lies.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much, I think that's all we need of the video. Thank you. All right. Now, can we deal, please, with the setup of your group of people who formed, as you put it, the TO of Kotor Varos? How many people did you have under your command?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you, the number kept growing as people were arriving, as the situation developed in the town itself. Certain villages had already handed over their weapons but the truce only lasted for a very short time. They said that they wanted to do away with all the extremists, the Green Berets, the Ustashas and the rest and that peaceful people could continue to live peacefully as they had up to that point. When people realised that certain villages had handed over their weapons they left them alone for a while. They went to the centre they are were moving about freely but after a certain period of time, they started arresting people, beating people and all the rest. All the rest they did. Now certain people realised they had made a mistake so they started leaving their villages and local communes and they started joining us so the number kept growing. The command itself consisted of a mixed group of Croats and Muslims, Bosniaks. I was appointed commander, Goran Markovic was my deputy, he was a Croat from Visevice. After the attack on Visevice, he went to Koljane [phoen]. My assistant was Bandalo, Drago from Bilice, and Puskaric. I can't remember his first name now. He was a good friend of mine but right now I can't remember his first name. Later on, the staff too, expanded and at one point included the local commanders too who stayed in their villages. So later on the staff grew also and had more members than originally.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Pause there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just for the record, and so that if Mr. Ackerman wants to make use of it for cross-examination, the footage, Mr. Inayat's footage, I know it has an exhibit number already, if you could perhaps indicate just indicate --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's part of P447.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That's it. That's all. Thank you, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Sir, you had local commanders who stayed in their village. Was there a strict command and control over all those villages? In other words, did they have to follow your and your staff's orders?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, naturally there was a respect but it was mostly based on the patriotic, on human considerations. Those people by and large knew me, who I was, what I was, what family I came from, what kind of jobs I performed because in our area people always respected those employed with the police or the military and so on and so forth. So people respected me because of what I was, who I was, who my parents were and what I did. So these people respected me, heeded and listened to me but to talk about some chain of command, no, it was based on patriotism, on purely human relations, of respects and appreciation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, at its height, or rather at the strongest point, how many people did you have directly in the village of Ravne working under your command?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, there were other villages too, not only Ravne. I mostly stayed there, well if I may call it the command of the staff later on I moved away, but when we add up all these villages, Doljani, Hadrovci, Radici, Ravne, Duratovci, Sokoline, Visevice, Postolje, I'd say some 300 or 400 people were under my care. The village of Vecici, well, they were reportedly on their own staff's command but they always held their own and they didn't really operate quite properly. Then on the other side, Drago was a local commander and because we couldn't communicate, because we didn't have any communicating equipment or anything, we were physically separated, you know, this is a huge territory, and especially Bilice, Visevice where Drago was, we -- there was the town in between us, which was controlled by the Serbs, and we held the village parts, and features around the town. So that it wasn't all in one piece. There were about three or four places where you could find larger number of people standing guard and performing other work, you know, food and, well, you know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Did you have any support in terms of manpower or arms from the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, unfortunately, I had absolutely nothing to do with anyone. We were completely surrounded. Both in terms of information, politics and everything else. And especially if you remember that Kotor Varos is between Celinac, Skender Vakuf, Travnik and Teslic municipalities, bearing that in mind we simply had no contact whatsoever. We didn't even have electricity so we couldn't watch the television or anything. So I even didn't have that possibility. I couldn't even learn anything from television. And I wasn't really paying attention to what was happening. Forget about communicating with somebody or helping. But sometime in late June or early July, we heard that there was a formation made of Croats and Muslims, a formation in Dubravci, or rather, Travnik, that is we heard that it was Travnik and later on we learned that its true place was Dubravci. Well, a certain number of guys in that group couldn't wait because they had been told to go to Kotor Varos to help us and so on and so forth but for some reason they never came but that is well known and I realise that later. But a number of guys disobeyed their command and they were so close and yet so far from their families and of course they wanted to know what was going on and they wanted to really know, find out what was happening to us just as we didn't know what was happening to the rest of people in Bosanska Krajina and Bosnia. And I thought that everybody had put up resistance in all the other towns in Prijedor, Sanski Most and Kljuc and so on and so forth. So we will see later on we'll come up with a solution but unfortunately that was not the case but I didn't know at the time that we were the only ones who were resisting. My apologies, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You're going too fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are running loose now again. Please slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I think we got the general idea from that. Can I ask you now about arms?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, my apologies but you have to bear in mind that I simply get too emotional and at times I simply can't control myself. My apologies to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You're by no means the worst, I can assure you that we have had here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I ask you now about arms? What sort of arms did you have in weapons?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, we had automatic weapons, the members of the reserve force, for instance had them, and they in part joined the resistance and we also had hunting weapons because we had our hunting society in Kotor Varos. There was quite a number of hunters and people made their weapons, they would take some pipings, pipes or tubes and make something -- some sort of single-barrelled rifles or pistols or some makeshift -- a certain number of our men had worked in Croatia and Slovenia, which made explosives so when they came home to Kotor Varos, they brought those back. So they made those devices. Or at times, they had bought the original TNT from Serbs. They bought the so-called soaps [phoen] hundred gram packages and used them to make bombs and so and so forth. But it was all based and light infantry weapons and to my knowledge there were about 2, 53 [Realtime transcript read in error "54"] machines -- 2 and 53 machine guns and there were a couple of more machine guns in the reserve force but otherwise it was all light infantry weapons perhaps a couple of Osa's which were bought from the Serbs but unfortunately somebody had cut off the cables so that they could not be activated.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I think we need to go back because what's come up is 2, 54 machines, I think you said two -- was it 2, 53 machine guns and is 53 the description?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I think that that is the make. That is how we called it. It was a Garonja and a Brno of Czech make.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you have any hand-held rocket launchers?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't have any hand-held launchers, not in the beginning. We had zoljas, which is a smallish anti-armour device which is used to act against armoured vehicles. We didn't have Osa's at that time. They were larger and we later on we captured some of them and we captured more machine guns, so that later on we had more machine guns, but this was later brought, a group of guys who were in Travnik brought these -- brought one also to Vecici I heard that one also had me brought with three or four charges but later on we captured mortars in combat [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the word that he keeps saying that's not making it into the transcript is Osa, O-S-A. That describes a particular weapon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sir, you have heard what Mr. Ackerman has just remarked. Have you been mentioning Osa in which case can you explain to us what it means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I mentioned both zolja and Osa. Zolja is a weapon used to destroy -- is an anti-armour weapon. I think it's -- that it's calibre is smaller than that of Osa. And Osa is similar but it's more powerful. It is a larger calibre. And I mentioned both these types of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you acquire any tanks or armoured personnel carriers?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Sometime in July, I think, I'm not sure, was it end of July or beginning of August, in an infantry attack, the Serbs were using a tank which broke in Vrbanjci, between Donji Vrbanjci and Zebe, roughly there, so they left it to us. But it was malfunctioning. However, they had mined it, removed all the anti -- all the weapons from it, and just left it to us. We couldn't use it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Did you have any functioning tanks working for you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: No, never, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Or what about APCs?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I already said only light infantry weapons. That is what we had. And that is how it was until the end.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So just to confirm, did you have any long-range artillery?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: No, we did not, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You mentioned how you captured various weapons. Did you as a group launch any offensive actions against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you, Your Honours, we simply gave it no thought. We were -- our purpose was to preserve the population, to safeguard it, to keep the territory we had, to begin with we had no weapons for anything to conduct any actions, we would have needed much more. However, the local commanders would at times engage in some small operations or sabotage activities in their areas. Personally, I was against it. And I was against it because whenever an operation was conducted and the Serbs would capture our innocent inhabitants, Croats and Bosniaks, in the town, those who had signed a loyalty, and every time something like that happened they would retaliate against the civilians and that is why I was against it and I was saying that such operations should not be conducted that we should agree what to do and later on we'd see.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to look, please, with you, at the description from the documents of various actions that took place during these months. Could you have a look, first of all, please, at P2157? This is dated the 14th of June of 1992, and it's from the 4th Light Infantry Brigade command and it records after the cleansing of the town of Kotor Varos, a part of the enemy forces and the Croatian and Muslim population escaped to the wider area of the village of Hadrovci. Was that, as you understand it, a reference to you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Hadrovci, the village of Hadrovci.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: As you understand it, is that a reference to the area in which you and your other colleagues were in?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, it does refer to us. This is the place, and it could be nobody else but us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Then the rest I think we can leave. Now, can you have a look, please, at 2165, I think it is? This is an extract from the minutes of the Crisis Staff held on the 22nd of June, which was attended by Lieutenant Colonel Peulic. And he apparently said that a group of about what he called 2.000 Ustasha were moving from central Bosnia as reinforcements for Kotor Varos. Now, did you ever see sight or sound of those 2.000 Ustasha, as they are described?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is propaganda in which the Serbs in the area engaged. I wish we had those formation there because we would have taken Kotor Varos with their help.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Now, can we look, please, at 217 -- P2177? This is the bulletin of the Crisis Staff dated the 26th of June, and it refers there in the second paragraph to this: Despite the fact that we are at war with extremists who will not surrender until the last man, events are unfolding to our advantage and our positions are better and better. The enemy is leaderless and in disarray, experiencing heavy losses. Their twin strong holds of Hrvacani and Bilica have been destroyed. Now, can I ask you what you know about this destruction of these two villages?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, as for Hrvacani, it was no strong licence hold. It was just people who lived in their houses. No formations, nothing. That was the first village that was attacked, shelled, and it happened immediately on the 13th or the 14th, but it was the first village which was publicly in front of everybody who could see it, was first razed to the ground by the artillery, and people yet managed to pull out under all those shells with minimum casualties. I think that six or eight civilians, that's what I found later, who did not manage to pull out, but the rest of the population pulled out and fled to the village of Cerkvisce [phoen] because there they had their relatives and friends and then some went to Hanifici and those who were younger went to Vecici and some of them went to Ravne Hadrovci whether they had any family there. So I can say under full responsibility that there were no formations in Hadrovci that there was no strong hold that there were guards looking after that territory but in Bilice, yes. There were considerable number of members. There was Drago Bandalo, he was the local commander and there were also people from -- from the town, who had joined there, people from Donji Varos, from Kotoriste and some even from Banja Luka, a guy had turned up there, he had either come to visit relations or whatever, and then eventually ended up in Bilica so that in Bilica yes there was a considerable number of members of the Territorial Defence but in Hrvacani there was absolutely nothing. It was just people who lived there normally, who worked there, and that they were shelled with large number of shells, one could see it easily because the weather was fair and I was looking through my binoculars from the position where I was, where I was moving, and I could see how house after house were shelled. The bulk of the shells went towards the minaret, that is the mosques. However, even after two days of shelling they did not manage to destroy it. They destroyed it later on when the infantry went in because then they planted explosives there and managed to destroy it so that is how things unfolded in Hrvacani but in Bilica so, so this is misinformation. Bilica did not take [Realtime transcript read in error "fake"] it and members of the TO were -- continued in Bilica and were there until the end. They were under attack at times but they never left Bilica.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: On the screen it says Bilica did not fake it should be take it. Very briefly, because there is a lot I need to cover still with you. What was the purpose then as far as you could see, for attacking Hrvacani?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: My personal opinion was that this was an attempt to demonstrate -- to give a demonstration of power, to show off, and to try to psychologically, to produce a psychological effect to show people what would happen if they didn't accept and sign loyalty to these authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now we see in that same bulletin that the -- they are asserting their control -- most of the municipality's territory except for the area to the left of the River Vrbanja from Vecici to Ravne. Enemy forces are currently in that area but they are encircled and under constant fire. Among their ranks they have many wounded and their food reserves are at an end. Yet despite this on the 25th of June the enemy extremists led by Spasa [phoen] and Sadikovic carried out a planned and well-coordinated attack on three places simultaneously, Vrbanjci, Revici [phoen] and Kotor. They suffered a terrible defeat with heavy losses. Now that asserts that you carried out a planned and well-coordinated attack. What do you say about that assertion?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have already answered this, and once again under full responsibility, I claim that no counterattack or rather a planned attack was launched from our side, because that is how our positions were. We have -- we didn't have the wherewithal. We wanted merely -- our purpose was to protect the population, to defend them and then see what would happen. This is just propaganda which they were carrying out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Sadikovic, the Prosecution hasn't got much time to finish her examination-in-chief. And you would be helping her very much if you contained your answers a little bit. In other words to be shorter.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In your answers, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I mean -- I will finish I have no doubt about that but it does help.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, sir. That's all I want to ask you. Can you look, now, please at P --

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honours. I will do my best to try to cut my answers shorter. My apologies to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: P2188, please. This is a report, Mr. Sadikovic, on the death of Lieutenant Colonel Stevilovic, who was the head of security for the 1st Krajina Corps, who apparently was killed in an ambush on the 5th of July. Did you or your group have anything to do with that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, personally, I had nothing to do with that action. Two or three days -- two or three days later, though, I heard about it and I was told the story by Stipo Maric so he was one of the local commanders who had a group and he -- who was slightly mischievous, if a good man, and who conducted this action. He always roamed around. I mean he just couldn't stay in one place. So I knew that that action was conducted but I didn't know about it then. I learned about it two or three days later.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you give any orders for any such ambush?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've already said it. I wasn't even aware of it, let alone issued the order. I learned about it only two or three days after it had happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Just one moment. Yes. Your Honour, perhaps we could break there because I want to show Mr. Sadikovic that video of the Kotor Varos, because we've reached that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So let's have a 25 minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just before we play the video, can I ask you, please, to look at one more document, very briefly, P2217?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This again is another one of these bulletins of the War Presidency. It states at the beginning that the Serbs armed themselves in any way they could, they did not have foreign support in this, unlike the other two ethnic groups which struggled to subjugate, expel or destroy them. Short answers, please, Mr. Sadikovic. Did your -- did the Bosniaks in Kotor Varos have foreign support to arm themselves? It can be answered yes or no, I feel.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you and the other Bosniaks intend to subjugate, expel or destroy the Serbs in Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now I want you please to look at the video which has already been exhibited at P510 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: While that is being prepared Ms. Korner in one of his statements he also mentions that -- about possible help, or money or weapons from SDA. Perhaps you could direct that question to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think I already asked him about the SDA but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If Your Honour can tell me which page of which statement you're looking at?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know, Ms. Korner, there are three statements and I wouldn't know exactly which one but -- you can put the question whether his group or resistance group --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I thought I did but I'll ask it again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did your group, sir, receive any assistance, financial or by way of weaponry, from the SDA party?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's the last -- the last statement, the one of 10th March, 2001, the last page. Go ahead. Can I ask you? Can you answer the question, please, Mr. Sadikovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. I can. We never, to the best of my knowledge, and I would have known had there been any form of support, financial or by way of weaponry from the SDA. There was never anything like that. It was just Serb propaganda going on all the time. There was no such thing happening. Had this been the case, things would have turned out differently, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So, you -- I think before we start playing the video, and there is a transcript, Your Honours, of this, I'm sorry, at -- it's in the bundle at -- I just passed it actually, when I was -- yes. It's P510. It's the same as the video, and it's in the bundle at -- in my bundle, divider 16. It comes after P2155.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, I think this is right, although you haven't yourself watched this video, in 1994, once you'd left Kotor Varos, did you see a film of news -- of a news report from Banja Luka Television?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. In 1994, I left on official business. I was in Croatia, Slovenia, Austria and Germany, and our citizens who lived over there informed me about the tape that they had recorded, because obviously they were interested in knowing what was happening with us down there. It was satellite footage and they recorded this on a tape, news from Banja Luka TV, about events in Kotor Varos. So I did have occasion to see that tape back in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If we now play the tape, then I'll stop and ask you various questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sound? That's it, yes. I can't hear any sound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. It's -- what I am seeing on my screen -- now it's changed. What I was seeing on my screen was the previous video.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's all part of the same video. It goes into the news.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But Madam Chuqing already had the footage that you would now be referring -- while I was --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That was the -- and this -- in computer evidence channel, and then the previous video, it is on video evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We are playing it on the computer but I'm told by Ms. Gustin that we don't control the sound so we are not getting any sound. Can we try playing it again? I don't know whether the --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. All right. I don't -- we've actually played this video before. There is -- the exhibit is the actual video but I think we will just go on. Otherwise, it will waste time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So, did -- first of all, is this, looking at this beginning bit, is this the bit that you saw -- I'm sorry -- is this the video you saw in 1994? Or do you need to see more of it before you can tell us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Sadikovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think it's the same tape that I saw, the same footage. And I'm familiar with the content of this particular tape so I don't think there is any real need for us to play the tape on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, but I want to ask you to look at parts of it because I want to see if you can tell us if you can date it? Can we go on even though it's silent?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can we just move on to the first --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Only a few kilometres from Kotor Varos are concealed house, Muslim extremists waited, hidden in ambushes and treacherously and perfidiously opened fire on the army and police troops [as interpreted]. In this perfidious attack one person was killed and a number of specials and soldiers wounded. Today, Captain Slobodan Zupljanin is also in the Banja Luka hospital. We first went to visit Captain Zupljanin who is currently recovering here. Captain Zupljanin: To be quite frank, I suppose that it could happen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Pause there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you know Captain Slobodan Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I did know him personally, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] But we never expected it at that place because the place we were to go to we were to meet at is much better for an ambush so that it came as a surprise. I'm aware, though, after all the situations in the west Slavonian theatre of war from which I had come, that the enemy will resort to any method, any means, any way, to destroy and liquidate us systematically step by step. Reporter: I repeat, this is not all that important either for Europe or the world but for ourselves to know who we are dealing with and to know who is waging war against us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Pause.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you know who that was? I mean I know it gives his name but did you know him, Mr. Stevandic or had you seen him before?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can we move on, then, please?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. I don't know this person. This was the first time I saw him on this tape.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Because all we can do is either win or vanish. Anyone else's victory would unquestionably mean that we would vanish and become extinct as a people. Reporter: Goran Tunic, a member of the special police detachment from Banja Luka was also seriously wounded yesterday. Tunic: There can be no more negotiations with them. They seem to recognise only the language of arms and that is how we should respond to them. Reporter Branko: They do it to their own and what they are prepared to do to others they show us day in and day out. Banja Luka television announcer: It is high time for you to part company with the extremists who endanger their lives -- saying terror. And we call on you to drive out any extreme individuals who have come to your villages as your villages could go up in flames because of them. In particular, we call upon the Muslim people not to be duped by Croat extremists who push Muslims in front of them to kill Serbs. You must realise that Croatian policy uses the Muslims in pursuit of its goal. Citizens go back to your homes, hand over your weapons and once and for all leave the extremists who wish neither you nor your children well. To all those who return their weapons, we guarantee absolute safety of their property and person says the appeal of the Kotor Varos Crisis Staff. Reporter Lagitak: Are under the control of Muslim and Croat extremists, the chief organisers of resistance in these villages are the notorious criminals --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Stop, I'm sorry, can we go back for a moment? No, to just the part before, sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Are under the control of Muslim and Croat extremists. The chief organisers of resistance --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Pause, please. Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, looking at that, I don't know whether that's meant to be Muslims or Serbs. Are you able to say?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm afraid I haven't quite understood the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: There is a picture of two people apparently in uniform holding a weapon. And they are talking, the commentator is talking about Muslim and Croat extremists. Are you able to tell us whether those are Serb soldiers, Muslims or Croats?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can state under full responsibility that these are Serb soldiers because neither the Croats nor ourselves had this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what's the weapon?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: In my opinion, it's some kind of a rocket or a mortar but it certainly is an artillery weapon of a rather large calibre.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Muhamed Debic [phoen] and Muhamed Sadikovic, they have many wounded in their ranks and they are running out of food. Vrbanjci, a recent Ustasha stronghold is now firmly in the hands of the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. On this occasion I want to point out that we have met with outstanding cooperation even among those people but unfortunately, our experience in two villages where we managed to reach an understand was that units of the interior ministry of the Serbian Republic of Krajina and members of my unit were fired on from these villages so that we had to respond appropriately. Reporter: Mr. Brdjanin, tell us, why did you come and how do you see the latest developments in the Kotor Varos municipality?

utterances.speaker: MR. BRDJANIN
utterances.text: Let me tell you my duty as the president of the Crisis Staff of the autonomous region is to visit all the fronts. I must admit most of the time I was in the corridor leading to Serbia but simply my visit, the reason for my coming here is that every Monday I must inform the presidents of Crisis Staffs about the political situation in this area. We must clean up our area which unquestionably includes Kotor Varos and Jajce and the most important battle which is under way and which I attended yesterday is the break through to Serbia. Simply, we can see for ourselves that there can be no more negotiations with those waging war against us. Those who took up arms must be defeated, hand them over and total Serb authority must rule here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you, that's all I need of the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, the only other question I have, Mr. Sadikovic, about it, is this: Can you tell us roughly when this film must have been shot? Because we don't have a date.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe this was the end of June or early July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, that's all I need on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, very quickly, can we look please at document P2001? This is a 1st Krajina Corps report dated the 17th of August, and in paragraph 3, it states that following a sabotage attack on a minibus in the area of Kotor Varos in which 13 of our soldiers were killed, the light Infantry Brigade from Celinac decided to take its revenge on the Muslim population around Celinac. Don't concern yourself with what happened in Celinac but do you know what this refers to, the sabotage attack on a minibus?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe this refers to attacks carried out by a local group from Vecici who had carried out reconnaissance and monitored the movements of those vehicles. They knew that another unit was taking over shift and they knew that they were soldiers on that minibus, not civilians, that's at least what I heard later. And that's when and where the action was carried out. In the Vrbanjci area. That's my opinion. I believe that's what it refers to.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did -- we've seen the map. Did you have any control or authority over the events in Vecici or in the other areas, Muslim areas, of Kotor Varos which were the, as it were, the other side of the town from where you were?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I've said before, I had no physical control because I was physically distant from this area. These were two or three distinct different areas. I could not physically be there. So in the early days, it was the local commanders who carried out those actions. This whole time I opposed those actions because there would always be retaliation as people from those areas were telling us. That's why I opposed this kind of attack, even against soldiers. That was the reason I was against it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. If you have 2239, please, now? And we'll see what you've just been telling us reflected in that report of the same date as the earlier one. This is another report, the 1st Krajina Corps, dated the 17th of August, to the main staff. If you go to paragraph 4, there is two paragraphs 4, in fact, but the situation in the territory, there is a very complex situation in the territory, in the general Kotor Varos area, Muslim Croat extremist groups operating, constantly sending in groups from the Siprage village area and the general area of Zebe [phoen], which are inflecting serious losses on our units in ambush operations. Before I move to the next line, were those two villages, as we can see from the map, the other side of Kotor Varos from which you were?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Siprage, the village actually, it's a local commune, including a number of villages, it's about 18 to 20 kilometres from where I was. And it's closer to Travnik. Our territory, that part of the local commune borders on Travnik municipality. So I had no contact or communication with that part of Kotor Varos municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then we see that it's reported that amongst the troops there is an ever-growing desire for revenge against the Muslim and Croat population, particularly against those who have buried members in their families. All right. Thank you, you can put that one aside. Can we now move, please, to part of the Exhibit 2248? It's the document -- it's the 71st meeting of the War Presidency. There is two documents contained in this exhibit. Actually I think it's one document in B/C/S. This is -- could you look at the one that's on the back? It's the 71st meeting, I hope. And in item number 2, it states that there was contact made by representatives of the village of Hadrovci with the command of a company in Vagani who wanted to hand over weapons in exchange for a guarantee of their safety. And this is dated the 3rd of September. Do you remember any negotiations like this?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: I remember, let me tell you, but I found out later from a local commander again, this is proof that I had no control over the whole territory. People play games. Some villages met, now were those informers, Serb informers or whatever, but those people without my knowledge, even without telling the local commander who was there, it may have been a group of two, three, four or five people from the village, so without informing their local commander, they went to negotiate with the Serbs, whether for fear, maybe they were afraid that they had made a mistake or something but to be honest I didn't know about it. I only found out later this could have given rise to serious difficulties among those people there. So when the local commander told me, I tried to calm the whole situation down. I tried to understand those people and tried to keep conflict from breaking out between those and the villagers.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours perhaps without showing it to the witness, two -- P2249 shows that apparently the negotiations referred to came to nothing. It's the meeting on the 6th of September. And the army will be put into action as planned.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, sir, there is a report which again I'm not going to show you, P2250, from this man Milos, dated the 7th of September which stated that the enemy formations in Kotor Varos area number about 3.000 members who are mainly positioned in the hills. Can I just ask you this: I know you've told us how many people you had. Would that -- your number plus the Croats that you knew of amount to 3.000 people? Resisters?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you, it's a far cry from the real situation on the ground. I wouldn't say there were as many as 1.000 people, including all the Muslims and Croats and the kitchen and everything -- everybody else. I wouldn't say there were as many as 1.000, let alone 3.000.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. All right could you have a look now please at Exhibit 2256? And could you be given at the same time or have ready 2257? This is a War Presidency meeting of the 17th of September, attended by presumably Slobodan Zupljanin, ah, yes, Captain First Class, briefing the War Presidency on the situation, no significant operations but an all-out attack on Vrbanjci took place in the morning, a village was also attacked and set alight and the people who happened to be there were most probably killed. Now, were you aware of that attack at the time that it happened?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you, Your Honours, this attack never happened, because Serbs held Vrbanjci throughout. It simply makes no sense. There was no attack on Vrbanjci, the village was in the Serb hands throughout. I'm completely unaware of this attack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are talking of the 17th of September or thereabouts, you confirm that on the 17th of September, the village of Vrbanjci was already in Serb hands?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. All the time, throughout.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then, please, I want to ask you about the event referred to in P2257. It's a meeting the following day. Now, Mr. Zupljanin, Slobodan Zupljanin, is briefing the War Presidency on an attack on the village of Serdari. Your Honours, that's not on any of the maps we've got so far so I'm going to ask that we hand in a map that's been prepared just to show that village. It will be P2328. Now, sir, Mr. Sadikovic, this I think was an attack, was it not, that took place by Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I found out later that there had been an attack on Serdari but this attack was carried out again by a local group with men who had come from above, from Travnik, a joint, a mixed group, of people from Travnik had come, Bosniaks and Croats, and allegedly, there was a depot or something like that there, and they therefore launched their attack on Serdari but there were no mortars because that depot wasn't there, and I found out about that later. It was closer to Bilica and Tesici and Bastine but yes, I heard about that attack. It did happen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, can we look, please, at 2264? This is another military document. It's the command of the 1st light Infantry Brigade in Kotor Varos and if you go, please, to paragraph 4, the commander, Mr. Novakovic says he's going to carry out preparations and mount an attack and we see the places that he's going to mount an attack?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's no use putting the document on the ELMO and when we are referring to paragraph 4 we can't see it. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The objective by unexpected and rapid actions using all combat and technical means to crush the enemy forces in Kotor, Ravne and the other places and then further actions to prevent enemy groups from carrying out actions against the army, the population and the facilities, and that's dated the 24th of September. Now, did such an operation start?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. That operation took place and it was a very difficult and broad operation with intensive use of artillery. I think it took several days. No, I don't think. It did last several days. I can't tell you whether it was four, five or six days but it did take quite a number of days. And the villages of Hadrovci and Doljani were razed to the ground by artillery and all the people took refuge in a nearby forest between Jakotina and Hadrovci, so the whole village with a mosque and all the other houses was destroyed, but luckily for us, the Serb infantry did not enter there and we repulsed the attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I want to move to the time when you left the area, and I think we can pick it up from a minute of the 1st of October, which is P2271. There, in the third paragraph, under item 2, Nedjeljko Djekanovic stated that representatives came from Sibovo where more than 650 people from other villages, including extremists were staying, by compiling lists of inhabitants the whereabouts of others, especially the men are to be checked. Bishop Komarica [phoen] had visited and suggested that everything be achieved by way of agreement with the involvement of the corps representatives, the people be transported and a stance be taken in all matters. Now, at the beginning of October --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, unless there is an objection I'm going to lead on this because I've got very little time left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Lead and then we see if there is an objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you attend at the beginning of October a meeting in some place -- four or five kilometres out of Kotor Varos town?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I did attend that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was that on the recommendation of Bishop Komarica, who was acting as it were as an intermediary between the Serb side and both the Croatian -- and the Croatian and Muslim resistance?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. And I'd like to seize this opportunity to really thank that great man. A true religious official who played a major role there. I would have never gone to these negotiations because I would have been afraid of it, but I talked with this priest and he gave me some guarantees and said that I could go and -- I could talk with him, and I really want to seize this opportunity because that was -- that was what was decisive in my consideration of the possibility of negotiating with the other side.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Was that meeting then attended by Mr. Djekanovic, Slobodan Zupljanin, Vojo Kupresanin, and some other persons, representatives of the military and also a representative, Mr. Bandalo, from the Croat side?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I will tell you exactly the composition. In addition to those you mentioned, there was Captain Balaban and there was Peulic, a member of the state security Stru [phoen], Mandela Simovic [phoen], and Mehmet Smajlovic, and I -- and I think Krevola [phoen] was also there. Four of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm trying to deal with this as shortly as I can, I'm afraid, Mr. Sadikovic, because of the time. I think from what you remember, Mr. Kupresanin was the main spokesperson from the Serb side and to you, he seemed to be in charge; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And effectively, did you raise the issues of guarantees for, if you all left and went to Travnik?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The other side was flexible enough, which surprised me, because they accepted the conditions, we are talking about the conditions under which we would agree to leave our municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I think there was then a later meeting with Colonel Peulic which you attended together with the Catholic priest and where you -- gave him the name of a list of around 2.000 men, women and children, that would form the convoy?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: A small correction. At that meeting, we agreed that we should compile a list with the full names of all those who would take that convoy, between 1.000 and 1500, not 2.000, and I didn't bring it then but we had simply agreed at that meeting that we would make the list of all those who would be leaving and that list contained about 1500 names of the citizens of Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you also go to Vecici, accompanied by the Catholic priest?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And with Peulic?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. If you look at the statement, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see after the meeting with Peulic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you go to Vecici?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED SADIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Since the local Vecici command did not accept our conditions, and the decision of the staff to go in this way, I thought that if I went to Vecici and used my authority, that I would be able to prevail upon those people and if I risked my own life, my brother's life, the life of my parents and everybody, I wanted to prevail on them that unless you risk something, then you couldn't gain anything or succeed in anything. However, between, on the road to Vecici, a group of people I knew was on their way. Now I don't want to go into details. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can lead him here Ms. Korner so that you conclude.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour I know there is a matter Mr. Ackerman wants to raise and can I -- literally, I just want to put in one more document tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman do you think you will require the entire sitting tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think probably -- I don't know. Probably not, Your Honour. Probably not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Would you be prepared to concede the first 15 minutes of tomorrow's sitting to Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Ten minutes would be ample.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Ten or fifteen would be no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we can stop here, send the witness back to the hotel and see what Mr. Ackerman needs to tell us. Do I have your indulgence, interpreters and technicians to stay for a further two, three minutes? Do you think you will cover that in two minutes, three minutes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Very quick, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The witness can be escorted. Thank you, sir. We will see you again tomorrow morning, when we hope to conclude with your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you want to wait until he's out, Mr. Ackerman or can you start?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I can start right now, Your Honour. It's a very simple matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: In line with your offer basically earlier this week, I think on Monday, and looking at what's coming to us the rest of this case, and considering how exhausted I am today, I don't know if you've noticed, I've even had trouble staying awake in court today, I would like to defer the cross-examination of those two main experts of the Prosecution, Mr. Brown and Mr. Treanor, until the Defence case. If we could do that, then I think we could get through this. That would -- I think that's acceptable to Ms. Korner, and that's my suggestion and my request. I don't need to go my further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know whether I'm overstepping at all but do you -- at the present moment, are you thinking of providing -- bringing forward also your own experts on the two areas that these two experts will be dealing with later on as Defence witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Depends very heavily on the cross-examination and how it works out, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know that in Stakic, for example, an expert was brought to balance what Mr. Brown had stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm fully aware of that and I'm even aware of that particular expert, and I think -- I will only know when I have finished the cross-examinations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is what is being suggested by Mr. Ackerman acceptable to you, Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, yes and no. First of all, yes. Subject to this, the matter I raised yesterday, which is we are going to be relying very heavily, pretty heavily, anyhow, on the expert testimony of Mr. Brown, and the expert testimony of Mr. Treanor, although Mr. Treanor in a sense is more just pulling the documents together but Mr. Brown is actually going to give you an analysis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think the expert evidence of both of them, I've gone through all the documentation that you have provided us with, and I think both experts are very, very, very important. One more than the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Treanor to a lesser extent than Mr. Brown and then there are parts in Mr. Treanor's reports which are extremely important, but others which are not that important.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The difficulty, Your Honour, arises -- I think Your Honours saw yesterday how is Your Honour meant to treat uncross-examined evidence for the purposes of the Rule 98 submissions? I think the Defence -- I think the only way of doing it is that the Defence will have to accept that that evidence is there, and they can't argue against it. That's the difficulty. Particularly, Your Honour, in respect of the schedules that were prepared to show what we suggest is the implementation of the Crisis Staff -- the regional Crisis Staff's decisions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I hear all of that and I think that makes a great deal of sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Let me just kind of play it this way. We'll see what we can do. If we can do it, we'll do it, and if we can't, we just can't, Judge, and I just can't put it any other way right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The only reason I ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Tomorrow may be better, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The only reason I asked Mr. Ackerman to raise it because I told Mr. Ackerman today that in order to fit in other fact witnesses we were going to reduce Mr. Treanor to two days and wait and see how long he wanted to cross-examine him for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was going to suggest that in any case to reduce him to two days.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: To two days, and Mr. Brown, I think we've left the three days for him because it's more of a complicated issue to follow through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's definitely a very important witness, Mr. Brown.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And Your Honour made reference to the general in the Stakic case who said he agreed with Mr. Brown's findings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not with everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. So, Your Honour, that's why we need to know, because clearly if Mr. Brown is not going to be cross-examined, then we will reduce the period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I personally, and I am more or less thinking aloud, I don't see much harm if any harm at all, if a cross-examination of Mr. Brown takes place before Mr. Ackerman brings forward his own expert, if he does. That's number 1. Secondly, with regard to Mr. Treanor, I don't know if Mr. Ackerman intends to bring forward an expert on the subject.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well -- what, I'm sorry, This is going to take a little longer but what's important is, if Mr. -- we can't wait. You see what I mean. We can, but -- for if Mr. Ackerman cross-examines Mr. Brown and then says I may be now getting an expert's report so there is no expert's report, and we can't consult Mr. Brown about any expertise, that's the difficulty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But what -- I will be consulting with my colleagues and we will come back to this because you caught me a little bit on the wrong foot and I don't know what to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's important, Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt, but it's important because of organisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I agree with you 100 per cent with you Ms. Korner but perhaps if we could for the time being restrict ourselves to your in chief which you keep to a minimum, and in a way, organise everything to try and make sure that we finish with the other witnesses, give and take some respite for Mr. Ackerman, I think it would be -- wouldn't be a bad idea. I don't know. But -- let me think about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because you caught me on the wrong foot.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can I then finally - I'm sorry, Mr. Ackerman - can I ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Can I just finish this one quickly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: What I had in mind Your Honour, and I think this was the logical thing, is if it's going to be deferred they would be the two initial witnesses in the Defence case. I'd finish that cross-examination before we actually went into Defence evidence so clearly they would be testifying before I would call any expert at all, clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would imagine so. But --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, that's right, Your Honour, then as I say the only problem remains the treating of that evidence for the purposes of Rule 98 submissions and Your Honour and Mr. Ackerman --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If it will be in the records, in the acts, it has to be taken into consideration of course, no point in discussing that because there is nothing which is in the records that is not being -- that is going to be neglected for the purposes of Rule 98 bis.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. But it shouldn't lose any of its cogency if I can put it that way, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Because it's not cross-examined. Then, Your Honour, perhaps I can have a confirmation tomorrow morning from Your Honours and Mr. Ackerman as to the definite that they won't be cross-examined because we have to start moving witnesses up. The difficulty there is some witnesses we haven't disclosed and we will fall foul again of the 30 day disclosure rule. So I raise that if we have to move witnesses up. The other matter is this: I don't whether this witness was protected or not. He's the man who has to come back who brought the diary with him. We would like to know has the Defence been given any indication when it's being translated because there is no point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: His book.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: His memoir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: His memoir, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: As Your Honour -- as you know they are not real quick and I asked that it be done by the 15th of July and I haven't gotten any complaint about that so I think it probably will be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. We will take that up. Again, I would like you, Madam Registrar, to extract what I'm going to say now and communicate it to the President. I wish to show in public my appreciation and that of my two colleagues for the constant and continuing cooperation of the interpreters, the technicians and the remaining staff of this Trial Chamber, which makes it possible for us to clear up certain matters in time but during extra time that they very kindly let us have. And I want to acknowledge that and I want the President of the ICTY to know that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
